rate_limits: No numeric HTTP request quota is published. Maximum 2 open WebSocket connections; clients must use jittered exponential backoff. Tibber recommends querying today/tomorrow prices only once daily and caching them.
example_request: curl -X POST https://api.tibber.com/v1-beta/gql -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "User-Agent: curl/8.7.1 MyTibberClient/1.0.0" -d '{"query":"{ viewer { name homes { id address { address1 city } } } }"}'
description: Tibber provides authenticated GraphQL access to account and home metadata, electricity prices, historical consumption and production, and real-time Pulse/Watty measurements via subscriptions. The published schema does not document operations for controlling EV chargers or smart plugs; connected-device data is offered separately through Tibber's Data API.
resolution_notes: auth_type: oauth2; Tibber explicitly requires an OAuth access token, using either a personal token or OAuth client: https://developer.tibber.com/docs/guides/calling-api. rate_limits: corrected; the same guide caps WebSockets at 2 and specifies backoff and daily price-query guidance. example: corrected; that guide requires User-Agent, Bearer, JSON, and POST. description: corrected; the current schema lists prices, consumption, production, and Pulse/Watty measurements but no charger/plug control: https://developer.tibber.com/docs/reference.
